items.claim: The isolation of Isa.44.23 as its own doxology row leaves a byte-true redeemer catchword undisclosed on BOTH of the row's seams, and its division-mark citation reaches only the rear seam while the same layer groups the three verses the disclosed rival joins.
items.evidence: Quote check: the row's splice matches its cited verse at byte tier, and the three summons forms are verse-initial there. But the redeemer root runs across both seams of this one-verse row in three consecutive verses, in three distinct inflected forms: כִּ֥י גְאַלְתִּֽיךָ (44:22), כִּֽי גָאַ֤ל (44:23), גֹּאֲלֶ֔ךָ (44:24) — a skeleton-tier root chain, NOT a byte-identical refrain (sweep: 21 verses book-wide carry the contiguous letter string, three of them consecutive here). The Jacob/Israel name pair likewise recurs at 44:21 and 44:23 (sweep: Jacob in 40 verses book-wide). Under the cross-seam cohesion rule a byte-true device straddling the row's own seam argues continuity against the row unless disclosed, and here it is precisely the strongest form of the rival the row concedes only on form grounds — the rationale argues the seam from addressee shift alone and never names the lexical hook. Second defect: the tier-3 division layer (single-witness) places a setumah after 44:20 and a petuchah after 44:23, so its nearest section unit is 44:21-44:23 — the mark corroborates the REAR seam only while the layer's own grouping runs with the rival; the row lists the petuchah as boundary evidence without naming which seam it reaches. Remedy: disclose the redeemer catchword at both seams with its tier named, and state the mark's direction.

items.claim: Both seams of Isa.44.24-Isa.44.28 are carried by the bytes: a verse-initial divine koh-amar frame with the tetragrammaton adjacent opens the row, an unbroken participial spine runs to the Cyrus naming, and a second verse-initial divine frame plus a division mark closes it.
items.evidence: Quote check: both splices match their cited verses at byte tier; the opening frame is verse-initial and names its own owner (the tetragrammaton stands immediately after the formula), so this is a divine frame, not the royal-messenger class that lives in the narrative zone. The participial spine claimed for 44:24-44:28 holds in the bytes: עֹ֣שֶׂה כֹּ֔ל נֹטֶ֤ה שָׁמַ֨יִם֙ לְבַדִּ֔י רֹקַ֥ע הָאָ֖רֶץ (44:24), then the frustrater/turner participles of 44:25, the confirmer plus article-prefixed sayer of 44:26, the sayer of 44:27, and הָאֹמֵ֤ר לְכ֨וֹרֶשׁ֙ רֹעִ֔י (44:28) — one chain of masculine-singular participles, each governing its own finite predicate. The two-site Cyrus claim verifies exactly (sweep: 2 verses book-wide, 44:28 and 45:1). Ketiv/qere: the span carries exactly ONE noted verse, 44:24, and the note is the verse-final doubled pair מי אתי מֵאִתִּֽי (unpointed ketiv beside pointed qere) — the row's verse-opening splice stops well clear of it, so no count or slice crosses the apparatus. Two minor notes, neither load-bearing: the phrase 'one of the row's ketiv/qere sites' implies a plural set where the inventory records a single noted verse in this span; and the redeemer catchword linking 44:23 to 44:24 goes unnamed at the front seam, though the row does disclose the shared divine-maker vocabulary and the shared Cyrus figure at the rear seam.
tier_citations: byte (both quoted splices verified against the source bytes)
tier-1 divine speech frame, verse-initial, owner named in the bytes

items.claim: The person-shift ground offered for the Isa.45.1 seam is byte-false at the cited verse: 45:1 speaks of Cyrus in the third person exactly as the preceding verse does, and direct second-person address begins only at 45:2.
items.evidence: The splice matches its cited verse at byte tier and the frame is verse-initial with the tetragrammaton adjacent, so the frame arm of the seam is sound. The person claim is not. In 45:1 every reference to Cyrus is third-person: the anointed is named with a third-person suffix, and the verse continues אֲשֶׁר הֶחֱזַ֣קְתִּי בִֽימִינ֗וֹ לְרַד לְפָנָיו֙ — a 1cs perfect governing a third-person suffixed 'his right hand', then 'before him' twice more. That is the same construction the row assigns to the verse it is cutting away from: הָאֹמֵ֤ר לְכ֨וֹרֶשׁ֙ רֹעִ֔י (44:28). The second-person address the row places at 45:1 in fact opens at 45:2: אֲנִי֙ לְפָנֶ֣יךָ אֵלֵ֔ךְ. So the person contrast does not distinguish 45:1 from 44:28 at all; the seam survives on its other, byte-true grounds (fresh verse-initial divine frame plus the setumah after 44:28, tier-3 single-witness), and the person argument should be re-anchored at 45:2 or dropped. Verified and unchallenged in this row: 45:4 is a NAMED-referent servant site (my servant Jacob / Israel my chosen), correctly kept distinct from the unnamed-figure zones and correctly left undecided; the ketiv/qere note at 45:2 is real (staged as an unpointed ketiv beside its pointed qere) and no splice crosses it; the two setumah marks inside the span are disclosed under the right type.
tier_citations: byte (quoted splice verified against the source bytes; person/suffix forms read off the pointed bytes)

items.claim: The twinning of Isa.45.9-Isa.45.10 stands on the bytes: two verse-initial woe onsets, the only two in this stretch of the book, sharing one interrogative challenge form and bounded by divine frames on both sides.
items.evidence: Both splices match their cited verses at byte tier and both woe particles are genuinely verse-initial. The woe lexeme is confined here to these two verses (sweep: 22 verses book-wide carry it; 45:9 and 45:10 are the only sites between chs 43 and 46), and it is the woe-oracle onset role, not the opening-indictment, self-exclamation, or invitation roles, and not the different woe lexeme that appears elsewhere in the book. The shared form the twinning rests on is byte-visible: 45:9 carries an interrogative he plus an interrogative pronoun, הֲיֹאמַ֨ר חֹ֤מֶר לְיֹֽצְרוֹ֙ מַֽה תַּעֲשֶׂ֔ה, and 45:10 repeats the same pronoun twice — one interrogative challenge across both verses. The bounding frames named by the row are real and verse-initial at 45:1 and 45:11. Division marks inside the span are disclosed under the correct type. Two observations that do not overturn the row: the potter catchword crosses its rear seam — the same word-form for 'his maker' stands twice in 45:9 and returns as וְיֹצְר֑וֹ in the answering frame at 45:11 (skeleton tier, prefix differs; sweep: 3 verses book-wide, two of them adjacent here), which the row implies by calling 45:11 a reply but never states lexically; and the tier-3 layer (single-witness) marks a division after 45:9 AND after 45:10, so it cuts with the disclosed rival split rather than with the twinning — worth naming as direction when the marks are cited.
tier_citations: byte (both quoted splices verified against the source bytes; interrogative he read off the pointed bytes)
tier-1 woe onset, verse-initial, role named
skeleton (potter catchword across the rear seam)

items.claim: The 'direct rhetorical question' that carries this row's form label is not in the Hebrew of Isa.45.11: the verse holds no interrogative particle at all, and the interrogatives it is said to answer sit in the two preceding woe verses.
items.evidence: The frame splice matches its cited verse at byte tier and is verse-initial with the tetragrammaton adjacent, and the divine title in it is a genuine title site (the plene title spelling reaches 24 verses book-wide, the defective spelling adding a 25th; sweep: 45:11 is the ONLY title site inside 44:23-45:25). The form claim fails. 45:11 reads הָאֹתִיּ֣וֹת שְׁאָל֔וּנִי — the he there is pointed with qamets, i.e. the definite article, NOT the interrogative he (contrast the interrogative he pointed with hataf-patah at 45:9, הֲיֹאמַ֨ר חֹ֤מֶר לְיֹֽצְרוֹ֙ מַֽה תַּעֲשֶׂ֔ה, and the same particle at 45:21); the first verb is an imperative-shaped form with a 1cs object suffix and the second, תְּצַוֻּֽנִי, is a 2mp imperfect with the same suffix. No interrogative particle, no interrogative pronoun, no question in the bytes — the question reading comes from the rendering, which the row itself quotes ending in an exclamation, not a question mark. The genuine interrogative challenge in this neighbourhood belongs to the woe pair at 45:9-45:10, i.e. to the unit the row says it is answering. Because the row's declared form category is argued 'on its opening rhetorical-challenge form', the label rests on a construal the Hebrew does not carry; with no morphology layer staged, an imperative-versus-indicative reading of the first form is a held question, and the honest ground is the summons-plus-command shape, not a question. Missed corroboration for the row's own rear seam: 45:13 closes with the postpositive signature אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת, a hosts-title speech closure that the row never engages, alongside the petuchah it does cite.
tier_citations: byte (frame splice verified against the source bytes; article-vs-interrogative he read off the pointed bytes)
form-class claim held, no morphology layer staged

items.claim: The stated ground that 'no addressee shift' marks 45:15 is contradicted by the pointed bytes, which shift from a feminine-singular addressee in 45:14 to a masculine-singular addressee in 45:15; and the row's koh-amar ordinal counts an enumeration it never names.
items.evidence: The frame splice matches its cited verse at byte tier, is verse-initial with the tetragrammaton adjacent, and the paseq disclosure is exemplary — count-only, single-witness, position expressly not claimed, and 45:14 is indeed the only paseq-bearing verse in the span. The addressee claim fails on the pointing. Throughout 45:14 the addressee is feminine singular — 'over you', 'yours', 'after you', 'to you' twice, all with the 2fs suffix — and the confession itself reads אַ֣ךְ בָּ֥ךְ אֵ֛ל, where the preposition carries a final kaf WITHOUT mappiq, i.e. 2fs. 45:15 then reads אָכֵ֕ן אַתָּ֖ה אֵ֣ל מִסְתַּתֵּ֑ר — an independent 2ms pronoun addressing God. That is a byte-visible addressee shift (2fs Zion to 2ms deity) at exactly the verse the row says carries none; the row may still keep 45:15 inside the reported confession, but it must argue that from the reported-speech frame, not from an absence the bytes contradict. Second defect: 'a third koh-amar frame' names no counted domain. The formula stands in five verses across this cluster (sweep: 48 verses book-wide; 44:24, 45:1, 45:11, 45:14, 45:18 here), so 45:14 is the fourth in the cluster sequence and only the third if the count is silently restricted to ch 45 — a restriction the neighbouring rows do not share, since 45:1 is called the second frame on a count that includes 44:24, and the 45:11 frame is given no ordinal at all. Name the counted object and the range, or drop the ordinal.
tier_citations: byte (frame splice verified against the source bytes; 2fs/2ms addressee forms read off the pointed bytes)

items.claim: The addressee contrast offered as this row's seam driver is half absent from the bytes: Isa.45.18-Isa.45.19 carry no vocative and no second-person addressee at all, so there is no 'address to the offspring of Jacob' for 45:20's summons to shift away from.
items.evidence: The frame splice matches its cited verse at byte tier, and the row is right to splice the causal particle with it: the formula is NOT verse-initial at 45:18, it stands second after that particle, and the tetragrammaton follows immediately, so the frame owner is divine and the disclosure is honest. The seam ground is not. Both verses of this row are first-person self-declaration; the only mention of Jacob's offspring is לֹ֥א אָמַ֛רְתִּי לְזֶ֥רַע יַעֲקֹ֖ב תֹּ֣הוּ בַקְּשׁ֑וּנִי — the phrase is the indirect object of a NEGATED report ('I did not say to...'), and the imperative in it sits inside the quoted speech that is being denied. There is no vocative and no 2nd-person verb or suffix anywhere in 45:18-45:19. The contrast the row draws is therefore between a real fresh address at 45:20 — הִקָּבְצ֥וּ וָבֹ֛אוּ הִֽתְנַגְּשׁ֥וּ יַחְדָּ֖ו פְּלִיטֵ֣י הַגּוֹיִ֑ם, three plural imperatives followed by a plural vocative — and an address that does not exist in its own span; the seam stands on 45:20's own imperative-plus-vocative onset alone, which is sufficient tier-1 evidence and should be stated as such. The disclosed rival is correctly named: the exclusive-deity formula does straddle this seam, standing in 45:18 and again in 45:21 and 45:22 (sweep: 7 verses book-wide carry it, 6 of them in ch 45). Also carried over from the neighbouring rows: 'a fourth koh-amar frame' counts an enumeration that is never named and that the cluster's own frames contradict — the formula stands in five verses here.
tier_citations: byte (frame splice verified against the source bytes; absence of vocative/2nd-person forms read off the pointed bytes)
tier-1 divine speech frame, non-initial after the causal particle, owner named

items.claim: The row's one recurrence claim — that the summons takes up 'the same declare-and-witness vocabulary as the earlier trial speeches' — carries no tier label, no digit, and no verse anchor, and the closing sentence grounds the row's rear edge in the work assignment rather than in the text.
items.evidence: The bounds themselves are byte-solid and I do not contest them: 45:20 opens with הִקָּבְצ֥וּ וָבֹ֛אוּ הִֽתְנַגְּשׁ֥וּ יַחְדָּ֖ו פְּלִיטֵ֣י הַגּוֹיִ֑ם — three plural imperatives followed by a plural vocative naming a fresh addressee — the splice matches its cited verse at byte tier, and the closing verse of the span is the justification verdict over Israel's offspring. The division layer is correctly reported as silent: there is no petuchah or setumah anywhere from 45:18 through 45:25 (the layer's own section here runs from the petuchah after 45:17 to the setumah after 46:2, tier-3 single-witness — worth noting as the rival grouping, since it spans this seam). The defect is the unsourced recurrence: the declare-and-summon vocabulary is real and checkable — הַגִּ֣ידוּ וְהַגִּ֔ישׁוּ at 45:21 — and the earlier trial-speech sites it echoes are identifiable (sweep: 6 verses book-wide carry that imperative, the trial-speech ones being 41:22 and 41:23), but the row names none of them, labels no tier, and cites no digit, so a recurrence claim carries no evidence and the verses argued outside the span cannot be mirrored in the evidence refs. Register: 'the end of the assigned range' argues the rear edge from the work unit rather than from the bytes; the honest byte statement is that the next verse opens a new taunt with a different subject and a burden-noun that is not an oracle header.
tier_citations: byte (quoted splice verified against the source bytes)
